content.value_statement: Production LangChain agents need clear architecture, memory, evaluation, and observability. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through LangGraph patterns, async tools, RAG, testing, and deployment.
actual_capabilities: Guides LangGraph state management, routing, and compiled graph patterns.
Outlines ReAct, plan-and-execute, and multi-agent orchestration approaches.
Describes memory options, vector retrieval, hybrid RAG, and reranking ideas.
Provides sample async tool, streaming server, retry, logging, and evaluation patterns.
Lists a production checklist for tracing, monitoring, caching, health checks, tests, and documentation.
limitations: Does not include runnable project files or packaged application code.
References an implementation playbook that is not present in this package.
Example snippets require adaptation to current library versions and provider accounts.
Does not validate credentials, vector indexes, deployment infrastructure, or security controls.

use_cases.title: Plan an Agent Architecture
use_cases.description: Map a LangGraph agent into state, nodes, routing, tools, memory, and evaluation steps before implementation.

use_cases.title: Prepare for Production Deployment
use_cases.description: Review async execution, streaming, retries, monitoring, caching, health checks, and documentation for a production agent service.

use_cases.title: Design a RAG Workflow
use_cases.description: Choose embeddings, vector retrieval, hybrid search, reranking, and memory patterns for a retrieval-augmented agent.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner Architecture Outline
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a new LangChain agent project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a basic LangGraph agent for my use case: [describe task]. Include state, nodes, tools, memory, and testing steps.

prompt_templates.title: RAG Agent Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Add retrieval and memory to an agent.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a RAG agent for [domain]. Recommend retrieval, memory, reranking, observability, and failure handling choices.

prompt_templates.title: Production Readiness Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Audit an existing agent before release.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this LangChain agent design for production readiness: [paste summary]. Identify gaps in async handling, monitoring, security, cost, and testing.

prompt_templates.title: Multi-Agent Implementation Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an implementation plan for a multi-agent LangGraph system with supervisor routing, shared state, tool boundaries, evaluation, and deployment checks.

output_examples.input: Design a customer support agent with RAG and streaming responses.
output: Architecture: intake, retrieval, tool execution, response, and escalation nodes.
Memory: short-term thread memory plus vector retrieval for support documents.
Production checks: tracing, retries, timeouts, streaming tests, and health checks.

output_examples.input: Review my agent plan before launch.
output: Main risk: missing timeout and retry boundaries around model and retrieval calls.
Observability gap: add trace IDs, LangSmith runs, latency metrics, and error counters.
Next step: write evaluation cases for tool selection, answer quality, and fallback behavior.
Use a supervisor node to route between research, synthesis, and review agents.
Keep shared state small and persist long-term context through a retriever.
Evaluate routing accuracy, source relevance, response quality, and cost per task.

best_practices: Use async model, tool, and retriever calls with bounded retries and timeouts.
Trace agent runs and collect metrics for latency, errors, cost, and answer quality.
Keep secrets in environment variables and validate all external tool inputs.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding provider keys, model credentials, or vector database secrets in prompts or examples.
Shipping an agent without evaluation datasets, integration tests, or rollback criteria.
Allowing tools to call external services without timeouts, validation, or audit logging.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps design LangChain and LangGraph agents with memory, tools, retrieval, observability, testing, and deployment practices.

faq.question: Does it generate a full project?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples, but it does not include a runnable project scaffold.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it help with RAG systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers embeddings, vector stores, hybrid retrieval, reranking, and memory patterns for RAG agents.

faq.question: Does it cover production operations?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes monitoring, streaming, retries, health checks, caching, testing, and documentation guidance.

faq.question: What should users verify before implementation?
faq.answer: Users should verify current library APIs, provider credentials, infrastructure settings, and security requirements.
